title: Clair de Lune (opening)
description: The third movement of Debussy's Suite bergamasque, the best-loved piece of French piano music: parallel thirds floating over a slowly sinking bass in D-flat major, 9/8. Learning it teaches voicing a four-layer texture, playing two-against-three duplets and shaping long tied notes at a whisper.

arrangements.label: Pro
arrangements.notes: Debussy's text for the opening fourteen bars up to Tempo rubato, with all four voices (melody in thirds, inner right-hand voice, the two left-hand voices), the duplets written as 2:3 tuplets, and the inner F of bar 13 shortened to a dotted quarter so it does not collide with the melody octaves.
teachingPoints: Bar 1: the left hand enters alone on the second eighth with F-Ab, then the right hand answers on the third eighth with F-Ab an octave higher; the left hand holds its third for the rest of the bar while the right hand moves on to Db-F.
Bars 3, 13 and 14 have duplets (two notes in the time of three eighths); practise them against a steady eighth count until the 2-against-3 feel is automatic.
Bars 5-8 the melody descends while the left hand walks down chromatically (Db-C, Bb-A, Ab-Gb, F-Eb-Ab); keep the inner voices (Gb, Eb, Db) softer than the top line.

Bar 9 restarts the theme as a climbing ladder of thirds on successive eighths: left hand Db-Ab in the bass, right hand F-Ab low (fingers 1-2), left hand F-Ab in the treble, then right hand F-Ab high before settling onto Db-F; bars 10-12 need the left hand to find the four-note Db-Gb-Bb-Db chord (5-3-2-1) right after the bass octave.
Bars 13-14 are the first swell: octaves in the right hand with 1-5, left-hand Cb-Db-F chord in bar 13, then settle onto Bb minor and back to pp before the Tempo rubato.
